title: dedicated-autoscaler: add burst throughput guarantees and improve utilization reporting
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: customers running Dedicated fleets have asked for more predictable short-term throughput during traffic spikes and clearer utilization metrics for chargeback and capacity planning. This PR introduces a burst throughput guarantee layer on top of the existing token-bucket autoscaler and overhauls fleet utilization reporting to surface per-fleet and per-node booked vs. used capacity.

What this PR does: - Implements a burst token reservation mechanism that guarantees a configurable short-duration throughput budget for high-priority routes. The implementation uses a per-fleet token pool with decay and accounting to avoid long-term capacity drift. - Adds throughput guarantees config to Dedicated API (fleet policy: burst_guarantee_qps, burst_window_seconds, priority_weights). - Improves utilization reporting: per-fleet moving-window utilization, per-node booked_vs_used breakdown, and new metrics exported to observability backend (redwood.metrics.dedicated.*). - Adds E2E tests and simulation harness for burst scenarios and integrates alerts for sustained bursting that exceeds allowed budget. - Updates docs and console UI strings for new policy knobs.

Motivation: Prior solutions allowed coarse autoscaling but could not guarantee short spikes for critical routes without over-provisioning. Burst guarantees let customers guarantee short, high-priority throughput while keeping fleet costs bounded. Better utilization reporting enables finance and infra teams to reconcile reserved capacity vs. actual usage.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc (Linear ENG-3421) reviewed by runtime and infra - [x] Unit tests added for token accounting and decay - [x] Integration tests added for prioritized burst routing - [x] Metrics exported and dashboards updated - [x] Docs and console strings updated - [x] Backwards compatible (old fleets ignore new keys)

Backwards compatibility: Defaulting all new policy fields to 0/disabled preserves existing behavior. Migration notes are in the release notes and the Linear ticket.

Related: ENG-3421, PM-812, SUP-1283.

conversation: Rafael Gomez (reviewer): Can you explain how booked_vs_used is computed and whether it includes cached KV memory? Requesting a short explanation in the comments and a test case.

Aisha Patel (author): booked_vs_used is computed as reserved_tokens/total_capacity vs. actual_consumed_tokens over the sliding window. It does not include KV cache memory; that's tracked separately. Added unit tests to assert booked_vs_used under a synthetic workload.
Priya Singh (reviewer): Observability team asks to prefix new metrics with redwood.metrics.dedicated. Please add mapping and update dashboards. Also flagged a flaky test in burst_scenarios_test.go.
Aisha Patel (author): Updated metrics prefix and mapping.yaml. Fixed test flakiness by making timing in harness deterministic for CI runs. Verified dashboards in staging.

release_notes:
- Dedicated autoscaler: add configurable short-term burst throughput guarantees (burst_guarantee_qps, burst_window_seconds, priority_weights).
- Improved utilization reporting: per-fleet booked_vs_used metrics and per-node breakdowns exported under redwood.metrics.dedicated.*.
- Migration: new policy fields default to disabled; existing fleets unaffected. See docs/ops/dedicated-burst-policy.md for upgrade steps.
notes: Performance: in internal staging benchmark, high-priority route p95 latency during burst reduced by ~20% compared to baseline while average fleet utilization increased by ~5% due to better token reuse. Operational note: sustained bursting that exceeds configured budget triggers an alert and automatic fallback to standard autoscaling.
